directions: Plant in fall in fast-draining, lean soil in full sun to light coastal shade, giving this vigorous groundcover ceanothus plenty of horizontal room since it spreads far wider than it grows tall. Carmel Creeper hugs the ground in a dense, glossy-leaved mat rarely more than two feet high, smothering itself each spring in small clusters of pale powder-blue flowers that draw bees and other pollinators. Named for the Carmel-by-the-Sea coastline where it was first collected, it thrives on neglect once established and resents summer irrigation, which quickly leads to root rot in heavier soils. It is a parent behind several golden-variegated groundcover ceanothus sports grown for brighter foliage.

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 move outdoors to a shaded location March-May. Fireflush performs best as a container plant brought indoors when temperatures drop below 55°F.

directions: Grow in bright shade to filtered indirect light in humus-rich, well-drained soil that is allowed to dry slightly between waterings; Fireflush is an outstanding rhizomatous begonia whose deep olive-green leaves are edged in maroon and covered in a dense coat of fine red hairs that catches the light like velvet. Small, lightly fragrant pale pink flowers rise above the foliage but are secondary to the dramatic leaf texture and color. It spreads slowly from a thick creeping rhizome and divides easily, and it is the parent of a popular spiral-leaved sport shown under related rhizomatous begonia entries in this dataset. Keep humidity moderate to high and water at the soil line to avoid leaf spot.
sources: American Begonia Society — Rhizomatous Begonia Variety Classification

common_name: Nippon Sunbeam Solomon's Seal (Yellow-Striped Japanese Solomon's Seal)

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring just as shoots emerge and set them horizontally 1-2 inches deep in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, spacing plants to allow the long arching stems room to display their foliage. Nippon Sunbeam is a variegated selection of Japanese Solomon's seal in which almost no two leaves match, each one streaked and splashed with irregular creamy-yellow longitudinal striping over a green background rather than the uniform edge of most variegated forms. Small, dangling, creamy-white bell flowers line the undersides of the arching stems in late spring, followed in late summer by clusters of dark purple-black berries. Established clumps expand steadily from slender rhizomes and benefit from an annual mulch of leaf compost; all parts are toxic if ingested.

common_name: Silver Lining Solomon's Seal (Silver-Striped Japanese Solomon's Seal)

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring just as shoots emerge and set them horizontally 1-2 inches deep in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Silver Lining is a more recently introduced Japanese selection distinguished by a single bold silvery-white stripe running down the center of each narrow, pointed leaf, rather than the marginal band or irregular splashing seen on other variegated Solomon's seal cultivars. Small white bell-shaped flowers dangle in pairs beneath the arching stems in early spring before the foliage fully expands. It forms a tighter, more compact clump than most Polygonatum falcatum selections, reaching only about a foot wide after several years, which suits it well to a shaded rock garden or the front of a woodland border. Keep soil consistently moist and mulch with leaf litter; all parts are toxic if ingested.

common_name: Bellingham Hybrid Lily (Turk's-Cap Pacific Coast Hybrid Lily Strain)

planting.note: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, with the base of the plant shaded by lower companions while the flowering stems reach toward the sun.

directions: Plant bulbs 4-6 inches deep in fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, keeping roots cool and moist while the flowering stems rise into more open light. Bellingham Hybrids trace to a 1920s USDA breeding program at Bellingham, Washington, that crossed the West Coast native species Lilium pardalinum, L. parryi, and L. humboldtii to produce vigorous, virus-resistant garden lilies with nodding, strongly reflexed, Turk's-cap flowers ranging from clear yellow through fiery orange-red, each petal heavily freckled with maroon spotting. Established clumps can carry a dozen or more pendant blooms per stem in early to midsummer and naturalize readily in a woodland-edge planting given consistent moisture. Mulch to keep the rhizomatous bulbs cool through summer heat, and avoid disturbing an established colony once it is settled.
